rows.description: A friend stands beside me when a bully comes and says "leave him alone". I feel brave and cared for. A friend's support shows me how to stand up for others, and together we go to a teacher.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, contempt, fear, trust

rows.description: I broke the vase and said the dog did it. My tummy feels heavy. At this age lying is often wishing it undone. A wise parent says "tell me the truth, I will not shout", and thanks me for honesty.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, deceit, fear, trust
related mind states: gratitude, guilt

rows.description: I lie because I am afraid of being scolded or hit. The fear is bigger than the wish to be honest. Homes where truth is safe get more truth; harsh punishment teaches children to hide better.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, deceit, guilt, trust
related mind states: fear, trust

rows.description: My parent believes me when I say I did not do it, even though I once lied. I feel respected and want to earn that trust. Being believed makes honesty feel like a gift rather than a risk.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, deceit, fear, guilt
related mind states: admiration, trust

rows.description: My friend lied and said I took his crayon. I feel angry, hurt and confused. Wise action: tell a teacher what really happened. The friendship may recover if he says sorry and does not repeat it.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: deceit, fear, guilt, trust
related mind states: anger, confusion, hurt

rows.description: I say I have a dinosaur at home. It is a pretend story, not really a lie, and I half believe it. A wise adult says "what a fun story, is it real or pretend?" Punishing imagination confuses it with deceit.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, deceit, fear, guilt, trust
related mind states: playfulness, confusion

rows.description: I tell the teacher "my mummy said I need not do it" to avoid homework. I feel smart and scared at once. Wise teachers stay calm and check gently. Learning that small lies are found out builds honesty.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, fear, guilt, trust
related mind states: fear, calm

rows.description: I peek during hide and seek or move my counter to win. I feel excited and a bit guilty. Winning feels huge at this age. A wise adult says "the game is only fun if it is fair", not "you are a cheater".
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fairness, rivalry, shame
paired view exists: Receiver (S546)
related mind states: playfulness, affection, guilt, excitement

rows.description: My friend moved his piece when I was not looking. I feel furious and say "cheater!" A wise action is to say "that is not fair, play again properly". Walking away is also fine if he keeps doing it.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fairness, rivalry, shame
paired view exists: Actor (S545)
related mind states: anger

rows.description: I want to beat my classmate at the race so badly that I start before "go". The rules can feel less important than winning. Wise coaching says "you can be proud if you try your best whatever happens".
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: deceit, fairness, shame
related mind states: pride
